[ASSISTANT_SAID] Paying builders for their dream home can be a complex process for homeowners, especially regarding progress payments under the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] This article provides a comprehensive overview of progress payments under the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract and payment schedule requirements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It covers frequently asked questions such as progress claim vs payment claim, how progress claims work, and how progress payments are calculated.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The article also explains the progress claim process, security of payment progress claim, and final progress claim, followed by the standard progress payment schedule in NSW and the role of the Security of Payment Act in regulating progress payments.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Progress payments are payments made by the homeowner to the builder during the construction process under the NSW HIA Lump Sum contract.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The payment schedule is usually divided into several stages, with each stage representing a specific point in the construction process.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Payment schedules ensure that both parties understand when payments are due and how much is due at each stage, helping to prevent disputes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Calculating progress payments involves applying the percentage outlined in the payment schedule to the value of work completed at that stage.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The final progress claim is the last payment request made by the builder and should only be paid once the homeowner is satisfied with the completed work.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The standard progress payment schedule outlines the payment schedule for a construction project, starting with an initial deposit and followed by progress payments at specific stages.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Security of Payment Act 1999 (NSW) ensures that payments for construction work are made promptly and fairly, allowing builders to make payment claims for completed work.
